title: “The sin of Judah is written with a pen of iron” — Brenton’s Greek prints no verses 17:1-4
summary: The KJV and the Hebrew edition quoted have four verses (17:1-4) before “Cursed be the man that trusteth in man”, including “ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever” (17:4). Brenton’s Greek page for the chapter prints no verse numbered 1 to 4; its first label is 5.
text: KJV Jeremiah 17:1: “The sin of Judah is written with a pen of iron, and with the point of a diamond: it is graven upon the table of their heart, and upon the horns of your altars;” Hebrew (WLC) 17:1: חַטַּ֣את יְהוּדָ֗ה כְּתוּבָ֛ה בְּעֵ֥ט בַּרְזֶ֖ל בְּצִפֹּ֣רֶן שָׁמִ֑יר חֲרוּשָׁה֙ עַל־ל֣וּחַ לִבָּ֔ם וּלְקַרְנֹ֖ות מִזְבְּחֹותֵיכֶֽם׃ KJV Jeremiah 17:4: “And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee; and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not: for ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.” Brenton’s Greek 17:5: Ἐπικατάρατος ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ὃς τὴν ἐλπίδα ἔχει ἐπʼ ἄνθρωπον, καὶ στηρίσει σάρκα βραχίονος αὐτοῦ ἐπʼ αὐτὸν, καὶ ἀπὸ Κυρίου ἀποστῇ ἡ καρδία αὐτοῦ. [Cursed is the man who has his hope on man, and will lean on him his arm of flesh, and his heart departs from the Lord] Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/17/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER17.htm.
reasoning: The KJV and the Hebrew edition quoted have four verses before “Cursed be the man that trusteth in man”. Brenton’s Greek page opens with verse 5 and prints no labels 1, 2, 3 or 4.
scope: T applies at Jeremiah 17:1-4 as an omission on the one Greek page named. This is a statement about one printed edition of the Greek; it does not show that no Greek manuscript has the verses, and the record does not claim the Greek denies that the fire burns.

title: “I am weary with repenting” — Brenton’s Greek has no such clause at Jeremiah 15:6
summary: The KJV and the Hebrew end Jeremiah 15:6 with “I am weary with repenting” (נִלְאֵיתִי הִנָּחֵם). Brenton’s Greek ends the verse “and I will no longer spare them” (οὐκέτι ἀνήσω αὐτούς) and has no clause about being weary.
text: KJV Jeremiah 15:6: “Thou hast forsaken me, saith the Lord, thou art gone backward: therefore will I stretch out my hand against thee, and destroy thee; I am weary with repenting.” Hebrew (WLC) 15:6: אַ֣תְּ נָטַ֥שְׁתְּ אֹתִ֛י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה אָחֹ֣ור תֵּלֵ֑כִי וָאַ֨ט אֶת־יָדִ֤י עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ וָֽאַשְׁחִיתֵ֔ךְ נִלְאֵ֖יתִי הִנָּחֵֽם׃ Brenton’s Greek 15:6: Σὺ ἀπεστράφης με, λέγει Κύριος, ὀπίσω πορεύσῃ· καὶ ἐκτενῶ τὴν χεῖρά μου, καὶ διαφθερῶ σε, καὶ οὐκέτι ἀνήσω αὐτούς· [and I will no longer let them go] Brenton’s own English for the last clause (https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/JER15.htm): “and will no more spare them”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/15/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER15.htm.
reasoning: The last clause of the Hebrew edition quoted is נִלְאֵיתִי הִנָּחֵם, in which the speaker says he is tired of relenting. The KJV puts it as being weary with repenting. The Greek printed has a clause about no longer sparing or letting go, and it does not mention weariness or relenting.
scope: T applies at Jeremiah 15:6 and to the closing clause. The record does not say what the Hebrew verb means. The record is limited to this verse.  This compares the wording of the texts quoted. It does not show which wording is original. The book is prophecy in verse and sermon; the comparison is of what the texts print, not of what the prophet meant beyond the words quoted. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined. The Greek quoted is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. It is not a critical apparatus and does not show that all Greek witnesses agree or which reading is original, and the record does not claim the Greek is a mistranslation of the Hebrew. English in square brackets is the researcher’s plain rendering, not a KJV quotation and not a lexicon entry.

title: Removal “because of Manasseh” — and “every one shall die for his own iniquity”
summary: Jeremiah 15:4 gives Manasseh’s deeds in Jerusalem as the reason the people will be sent into all the kingdoms of the earth. Jeremiah 31:29-30 says that in those days the saying about fathers eating sour grapes will end and each will die for his own iniquity.
text: KJV Jeremiah 15:4: “And I will cause them to be removed into all kingdoms of the earth, because of Manasseh the son of Hezekiah king of Judah, for that which he did in Jerusalem.” KJV 31:29-30: “In those days they shall say no more, The fathers have eaten a sour grape, and the children's teeth are set on edge. But every one shall die for his own iniquity: every man that eateth the sour grape, his teeth shall be set on edge.” Hebrew (WLC) 15:4: וּנְתַתִּ֣ים [לִזְוָעָה כ] (לְזַֽעֲוָ֔ה ק) לְכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכֹ֣ות הָאָ֑רֶץ בִּ֠גְלַל מְנַשֶּׁ֤ה בֶן־יְחִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה עַ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ Hebrew (WLC) 31:29-30: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם לֹא־יֹאמְר֣וּ עֹ֔וד אָבֹ֖ות אָ֣כְלוּ בֹ֑סֶר וְשִׁנֵּ֥י בָנִ֖ים תִּקְהֶֽינָה׃ כִּ֛י אִם־אִ֥ישׁ בַּעֲוֹנֹ֖ו יָמ֑וּת כָּל־הָֽאָדָ֛ם הָאֹכֵ֥ל הַבֹּ֖סֶר תִּקְהֶ֥ינָה שִׁנָּֽיו׃ ס Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 15:4: Καὶ παραδώσω αὐτοὺς εἰς ἀνάγκας πάσαις ταῖς βασιλείαις τῆς γῆς, διὰ Μανασσῆ υἱὸν Ἐζεκίου βασιλέως Ἰούδα, περὶ πάντων ὧν ἐποίησεν ἐν Ἱερουσαλήμ. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Jeremiah 38:29-30: Ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις οὐ μὴ εἴπωσιν, οἱ πατέρες ἔφαγον ὄμφακα, καὶ οἱ ὀδόντες τῶν τέκνων ᾑμωδίασαν. Ἀλλʼ ἢ ἕκαστος ἐν τῇ ἑαυτοῦ ἁμαρτίᾳ ἀποθανεῖται, καὶ τοῦ φαγόντος τὸν ὄμφακα αἱμωδιάσουσιν οἱ ὀδόντες αὐτοῦ. Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER15.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER31.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/15/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/31/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER15.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER38.htm.
reasoning: 15:4 uses בִּגְלַל (“on account of”) with Manasseh, a king who had died before this word, as the cause of a judgment on the present people. 31:29-30 says the proverb that children suffer for what fathers ate will no longer be said, and that each dies for his own עָוֹן. The Hebrew and the Greek agree with the KJV in both places.
scope: No tag: the Hebrew, the Greek and the KJV agree. The statements can both stand: 31:29-30 is set in “those days”, a later time than 15:4, and the next verses of chapter 15 also charge the present people with their own turning away (15:6). The text does not say that Manasseh’s sin alone caused the removal. The record does not say the passages are in error.
